gen_risks.description: Recurring extreme flood events could overwhelm microfinance providers' capital buffers and lead to widespread borrower default across vulnerable agricultural and rural communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish and capitalize the Climate Risk Fund (CRF) to provide post-disaster contingent liquidity and transfer extreme risk through an international parametric reinsurance backstop.
gen_risks.evidence: a 1-in-a-20-year flood, as an example, would impact 705,000 borrowers and US$189 million in lending.

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic instability and persistent inflation in Pakistan could impair borrower repayment capacity, degrading microfinance provider asset quality and curtailing overall lending.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide tailored liquidity facilities (IAL and CLF) on market-based terms while monitoring MFP capital adequacy and macroeconomic stress indicators.
gen_risks.evidence: The impact of these shocks was exacerbated by the macroeconomic crisis brewing since late 2019.

gen_risks.description: Climatic shocks can trigger a surge in non-performing loans (NPLs), leading to rapid capital adequacy erosion and liquidity impairment for Microfinance Banks (MFBs).
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Contingent Liquidity Facility (CLF) funds after qualifying flood events to enable MFPs to restructure loans and issue fresh recovery loans.
gen_risks.evidence: NPLs of MFBs in flood impacted areas surged by 25.7 percent... resulted in the rapid erosion of liquidity and capital of the MFBs.

gen_risks.description: Structural disintermediation away from agricultural sector lending by MFPs increases financial exclusion for small farmers and pushes them toward exploitative informal debt sources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Pre-Climate Event Innovative Agricultural Liquidity (IAL) product to bundle agricultural loans with precision advisory support from agritech companies.
gen_risks.evidence: have led to a structural shift in the sector, which is gradually pivoting away from agriculture.

gen_risks.description: Rapid expansion of short-term urban nano loans for consumption smoothing risks shifting microfinance away from productive investment and over-indebting vulnerable borrowers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incentivize MFPs through CRF liquidity allocations to expand productive lending in climate-smart agriculture and microenterprises.
gen_risks.evidence: Nano loans have grown by 342 percent... alarming pivot away from lending for productive purposes to consumption smoothing.

gen_risks.description: Structural gender disparities, loan officer biases, and post-disaster mobility constraints could prevent female borrowers from accessing emergency disaster recovery finance equitably.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate that at least 55% of beneficiaries from CRF liquidity are women, enforce higher borrowing costs for non-compliant MFPs, and provide loan officer gender-bias training.
gen_risks.evidence: post-disaster assistance often fails to reach women equitably... target that at least 55% of the beneficiaries of MFPs benefitting from CRF liquidity are women

gen_risks.description: Delays in negotiating, executing, and legally registering the Trust Deed between Ministry of Finance and SBP could delay project effectiveness and fund capitalization.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ensure proactive legal coordination between the Ministry of Finance, State Bank of Pakistan, and World Bank legal teams to complete Trust Deed execution and registration.
gen_risks.evidence: The Trust Deed, in form and substance acceptable to the Association, has been executed... and registered in accordance with the legal requirements

gen_risks.description: Failure or delay in securing national budget allocation for counterpart local currency requests could prevent disbursements under Category 2 of the credit line.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate required PKR budget allocations directly into the national fiscal budget planning process managed by the Ministry of Finance and SBP.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawals can take place under Category 2 until the Recipient has ensured... sufficient amount in its currency has been requested in its budget allocation

gen_risks.description: Volatile pricing or limited availability in international reinsurance markets could make securing annual parametric insurance backstop coverage unviable for the CRF.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct annual technical and financial reviews by the CRF Oversight Committee, leveraging GSFF grant funds and CRF investment income to support premium payments.
gen_risks.evidence: The final amounts are subject to an annual decision by the CRF Oversight Committee on insurance purchases, following technical and financial review

gen_risks.description: Inaccurate risk modeling or inappropriate parametric trigger design could cause the CRF to fail to release post-disaster liquidity during localized flood shocks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish dual independent trigger mechanisms verified by independent third-party risk modeling firms and detailed rigorously in the Project Operating Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: The definition of parametric indices, triggers, and a post event loss calculation (PELC) method, as part of the risk modelling, will be central

gen_risks.description: Geographical clustering of agricultural and SME micro-loans could cause cumulative localized environmental degradation through increased chemical runoff and water contamination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply SBP's Environmental and Social Management System screening processes and enforce negative lists and guidelines in accordance with the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan.
gen_risks.evidence: clustering of loans in geographical areas (such as in the cotton belt) where project interventions may increase use of fertilizers, pesticides and other chemicals.

gen_risks.description: Delays or operational difficulties in establishing effective partnerships between MFPs and Agriculture Technology Companies (ATCs) could impede deployment of the IAL product.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute the Agriculture Finance Innovation Challenge (AFIC) through SBP to pre-select a panel of qualified ATCs for seamless bundling with MFP loans.
gen_risks.evidence: MFPs that avail the IAL product will have to partner with at least one ATC selected under the AFIC.

gen_risks.description: Operational bottlenecks or administrative slow-downs within SBP governance structures could prevent post-flood liquidity deployment to MFPs within the target 60-day window.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define streamlined operational TORs and delegation frameworks between the CRF Oversight Committee and Working Committee in the Project Operating Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: CRF liquidity which is deployed to originate loans within 60 days of qualifying floods (percentage)

gen_risks.description: Competing regulatory priorities or staffing constraints within SBP could create administrative bottlenecks in performing Trustee duties for the CRF Trust.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize SBP's dedicated microfinance department and leverage existing operational expertise gained from implementing the Financial Inclusion and Infrastructure Project.
gen_risks.evidence: CRF will be established and capitalized as a Trust owned by the GoP and managed by the SBP as the Trustee

gen_risks.description: Lack of coordination among international financial institutions (ADB, IFC, WB, FCDO, GIZ) could lead to overlapping de-risking structures and market fragmentation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align interventions under the shared 10-year microfinance sector vision and enforce clear market segmentation between ADB's WIF guarantee structure and WBG facilities.
gen_risks.evidence: clear market segmentation so that the proposed WBG guarantee structure compliments (rather than competes) with the ADB structure.

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk is Substantial. The political context in Pakistan remains fluid. However, there has been significant decline in political uncertainty and associated policy instability in recent months, especially in the backdrop of the general elections. Given that a new government took the helm recently and the fact that policy priorities are still being defined, political risks, in particular in the context of the project, remain substantial.
gt_risks.mitigation: In the implementation stage, the risks will be mitigated through frequent monitoring and oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is High. While fiscal consolidation measures have supported short-term stabilization, macroeconomic risks remain high amid a high debt burden (72 percent of GDP), heavy financial sector exposure to government debt, large external financing needs, weak confidence, and little progress with structural reforms. Significant risks include potential worsening of external conditions, further natural disasters, and a slowdown or reversals in policy adjustment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Risks are partly mitigated by government commitment to implementation of reforms under the ongoing International Monetary Fund program, World Bank support to structural policy reforms in the fiscal and power sectors, strong government commitment to the reforms supported by the operation, and the availability of dedicated World Bank technical assistance to implement key reforms.
